card.title: Free-body diagrams: the forces acting on one body

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A free-body diagram isolates ONE body and draws every force acting on it: the applied force F, friction f, its weight mg and the normal reaction R. Arrows start at the body's centre and their lengths stand for the magnitudes, so the diagram is the equation before the algebra.

figure.caption: Free-body diagram — F applied, f friction, mg weight and R the normal reaction; the net force is their vector sum.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: ΣF = ma;  along x: F − f = ma;  along y: R − mg = 0  ⇒  R = mg

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Draw one body at a time, in an inertial frame, including every contact and field force exactly once — no more and no less.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: On a smooth floor f = 0 so a = F/m; if F is smaller than the limiting friction the body stays at rest and friction self-adjusts to f = F.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The diagram shows only the forces ON this body; the third-law partners it exerts on the surroundings act on different bodies and must be drawn separately.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Vertical equilibrium: R = mg.  Horizontal: F − f = ma  ⇒  a = (F − μR)/m = F/m − μg

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Normal reaction first, then friction f = μR, then a = (F − f)/m; never start from acceleration.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Draw the free-body diagram of a block pulled along a rough horizontal surface and derive its acceleration.
